title: Pre-op anesthesia assessment
what: The anesthetist gets to know you, asks about your health, and chooses the safest anesthesia for your surgery.
why: Before any surgery or procedure under general anesthesia, sedation, or spinal anesthesia.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes; sometimes a few days before, sometimes the day before or the day of surgery
tell_doctor: All your medicines, including vitamins and herbs
Heart, lung, or kidney disease, or diabetes
Snoring or pauses in breathing during sleep
How past anesthesia went for you and your relatives

prepare.title: List
prepare.text: Write down your medicines with doses and your questions in advance.

prepare.title: Documents
prepare.text: Gather your test results, ECG, and doctors' reports.

prepare.title: Questions
prepare.text: Ask what kind of anesthesia it will be, when to stop eating, and what to do with your medicines that morning.

steps: The anesthetist asks about your health and past surgeries
Your heart and lungs are checked, and your blood pressure measured
Your mouth and neck are checked to see how easy breathing support will be
Your test results are reviewed. Sometimes more are ordered
The type of anesthesia is suggested and the risks explained
You are told when to stop eating and drinking and what to do with medicines
You sign a consent form for anesthesia
feel: It is just a conversation and a short exam, with no pain
Feeling nervous is normal. Ask anything that worries you
after: Write down the time after which you must not eat or drink
Do with your medicines only what the doctor said
If you get ill before surgery, call the clinic

faq.q: Can I choose the type of anesthesia?
faq.a: You can share your wishes. In the end, the anesthetist chooses the safest option for you.
A loose tooth or denture can get in the way of placing the breathing tube. The doctor will plan for it.

reminders.text: Anesthesia assessment tomorrow. Bring your test results, ECG, and medicine list, and write down your questions.
